title: Mode
summary: The mode is the value that appears most often in a dataset. Explore how to spot the most frequent value — and what to do when there is a tie or no mode at all.

compareCandidate.label: Mode vs. mean
compareCandidate.description: The mode is the most frequent value (pure counting); the mean is the fair-share value (pure arithmetic). Mode works even for words and colors.

processes: Counting how often each value appears
plainLanguageExplanation: The mode is the value that shows up most often in a dataset. Count how many times each value appears and the one with the highest count wins. In 2, 3, 3, 3, 5, the mode is 3. Two values tied for most make two modes (bimodal); if every value appears the same number of times, there is no mode. Unlike the mean and median, the mode works for any kind of data — it can be a number, a color, or a food, which makes it perfect for survey answers.

keyFacts.label: None
keyFacts.value: All values equal count = no mode

keyFacts.label: Special
keyFacts.value: Works for words and categories too

whyItMatters: Retailers care about the mode (best-selling size), survey makers care about the mode (most common answer), and city planners care about the mode (busiest hour). It answers the 'most popular' question no other statistic can.
didYouKnow: 'Mode' and 'modern' share a root from Latin 'modus' — meaning measure, manner, or way. A mode is 'the way it most commonly is'.
compareReason: Students expect every summary to need arithmetic — comparing the count-based mode with the arithmetic mean shows the mode works for non-numbers too.
